main_body: 4x3 grid of riveted blue-grey metal floor/wall panels (terrain patch) with cyan lights in the right column
top_band: none. This is a tiling terrain patch, not a standing object. Column x=47 shows only a dark base (L=50) with 1-row highlight/shadow lines every 16 rows (L=93 and L=70) that mark panel edges.
evidence: The kind is terrain (autotile-style block), so the standing-object 3/4 contract does not apply. The panels are bevelled plates with light top-left edges and dark bottom-right edges, and the centre column has recessed hatches with inner shadows. No receding side faces and no standing object that needs a visible top. It reads acceptably as a tileable surface.

style.evidence: Measured: 9 colours, median 6 per tile, 0% flat-fill coverage, 0% neutral dark edge pixels (tinted blue-slate outlines). This is on par with the paving reference (7 colours, median 7, 80% neutral outlines) and well below the grass reference (80 colours, median 26). The metal ramp has about 5 steps (dark base, mid slate, light slate, highlight, cyan accent), with rivets, bevels and recessed hatches giving some texture. The outline is a dark blue-slate tint of the material, not black. It is simpler than the grass but comparable to the paving and not sticker-like.
